title: Session records, review points and handover to a health professional
audience: Consultants who keep session records for general eating-habit support, review goals with clients and hand over to a health professional when a referral is needed.
learningOutcomes: Write a session note that records what was discussed, what the client chose and what was referred, without clinical labels.
Set review points and stop points with the client for each habit goal.
Prepare a handover to a health professional with the client's consent and only the information that is needed.
Describe how records are kept, shared and retained under the business policy.

instruction.heading: Why records matter in a general consult
instruction.body: A short, accurate session note protects the client and the practitioner. It shows what was discussed, what the client chose to work on, what was explained about the limits of the service and whether any referral was made. A good note is factual and written in plain words. It does not diagnose, it does not repeat rumours or assumptions, and it does not record more health detail than the client has agreed to share and the purpose requires.

instruction.heading: Writing a session note
instruction.body: Record the date, the duration and who was present. Note the goals the client chose, the habits agreed for the next period and the review date. Record any limits statement given and any referral discussed. Where the client used a particular phrase about their feelings or experience, you may quote it, but keep quotations short and relevant. Avoid labels such as the name of a condition, a judgement about the client's character or a comment about their body. Sign or initial the note in the approved system the same day.

instruction.heading: Setting review points and stop points
instruction.body: For each habit goal, agree a review point, usually a date or number of sessions, when the client and the practitioner look at what has happened and decide whether to continue, change or stop the habit. Agree stop points as well. A stop point is a sign that the habit plan should pause and the client should see a health professional, such as a new symptom, a new medication, a pregnancy, distress about food or a change the client did not expect. Record the review and stop points in the session note and show them to the client. Do not set a target for weight loss or a timeline for an outcome.

instruction.heading: Handover to a health professional
instruction.body: When a referral is made, prepare a handover only with the client's informed consent. Share the information that the receiving professional needs for the referral, such as the reason for referral and the relevant general goals, and nothing else. Use the business's approved referral template where one exists. Do not send a full record without the client's agreement and a stated purpose. Record that the handover was made, what was shared, the date and to whom. The handover template, and the rules for sharing health information, are UNCONFIRMED in this draft and must be confirmed by the reviewer.

instruction.heading: Storage, access and retention
instruction.body: Keep session records in the approved system, with access limited to the people who need them for the service. Do not keep copies on personal devices or in messages. Follow the retention period set by the business policy, and follow the process for correcting or deleting records when a client asks. The retention period and the legal requirements for records are UNCONFIRMED in this draft and must be confirmed by the reviewer.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor should check a sample of session notes and handover records against this lesson. A competent practitioner can write a factual session note, set review and stop points, prepare a consented handover with only the needed information and keep records in the approved system. Escalate any request to share records with a third party, any record that suggests the client is at risk and any note that contains information the client has not agreed to share.

procedure: Write the session note the same day in the approved system, with the date, attendees and duration.
Record the client's chosen goals, the agreed habits, the review date and the stop points.
Record any limits statement and any referral discussed, using plain words and no clinical labels.
Where a referral is made, confirm the client's consent and prepare the handover with only the needed information.
Record the handover, what was shared, the date and the recipient.
Store the note in the approved system and check access settings.

workedExamples.situation: A client's review is due. They say they have kept to a habit of eating breakfast on most days, but they feel very stressed and have stopped sleeping well.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you record and what do you do next?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the habit progress in the client's terms. Treat the sleep and stress comments as a stop point and check whether they describe a referral situation from the earlier lessons. Do not set a new target for weight. If the client has any health concern, suggest they speak with their health professional, record the advice and agree a shorter review point.

workedExamples.situation: A client agrees to a referral to their general practitioner and asks you to send the GP your full session notes.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not send the full notes by default. Ask the client what they want the GP to know, confirm the purpose and the consent in writing, and share only the reason for the referral and the agreed general goals. Use the approved referral template where one exists. Record what was shared, the date and the recipient.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved referral and handover template, once confirmed
Written consent form for sharing information with a health professional
Approved client record system with access controls

commonErrors.error: Writing judgemental or clinical labels in the session note.
commonErrors.prevention: Record what the client said and did, in plain words, and leave out labels and judgements.

commonErrors.error: Sending the full record to a health professional without the client's specific agreement.
commonErrors.prevention: Share only the information the referral needs, with the client's written consent and a stated purpose.

commonErrors.error: Setting a weight target or a timeline as the review point.
commonErrors.prevention: Use review and stop points based on the client's chosen habits and wellbeing, and do not set outcome targets.

commonErrors.error: Keeping copies of notes on a personal device.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep records only in the approved system and remove any working copies.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Health information is sensitive. Rules on sharing, storing and retaining it apply. The specific rules for this business are UNCONFIRMED in this draft and must be confirmed by the reviewer.

Completing this lesson does not give authority to keep clinical records, to diagnose or to treat, and the records kept under this lesson are not clinical notes unless the business and the reviewer confirm that they are.

qualityStandard: Each session note has a date, the goals chosen by the client, the agreed habits, the review date and the stop points.
Any referral is recorded, and the handover contains only the information the referral needs, with consent.
No clinical labels or outcome targets appear in the note.
All records are stored in the approved system and are accessible only to people who need them.
documentationEvidence: Session note in the approved system, with the date, goals, habits, review date and stop points.
Written consent for each handover, with the date and the recipient.
Record of each handover, showing what was shared.
summary: Write factual, plain-language session notes with no clinical labels.
Set review and stop points based on the client's chosen habits and wellbeing, not on outcome targets.
Hand over only the information a referral needs, with the client's written consent.
Store records only in the approved system and follow the retention policy.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which is the best way to write a session note?
options: Write a factual note in plain words that records goals, agreed habits, review date and any referral.
Write a short label for the client's condition so the next consultant understands quickly
Write a note only when the client is happy with the session

knowledgeChecks.question: A client agrees to a referral. What should be shared with the health professional?
options: The full session notes, so the professional has everything
Only the information the referral needs, with the client's written consent.
Nothing, because the client can explain the referral to the professional themselves

knowledgeChecks.question: What is a stop point in a habit plan?
options: The weight at which the client has reached their target
A sign, such as a new symptom or distress about food, that the habit plan should pause and the client should see a health professional.
The date on which the client must stop attending sessions
